key_insight: SayWhen enables early speech by releasing only task-directed commitments supported across candidate continuation plans, with a persistent veto for invalidating transcript updates.
engineering_relevance: Voice-agent designers can explicitly trade early-response coverage against semantic compatibility rather than simply speaking the most likely next response.
method: Select a shared task-directed act across typed continuation plans.
Control speech release and persistently veto playback when new transcript evidence invalidates the candidate.
Measure supported pre-endpoint releases without scored incompatibility using regret-free early speech (RFES).
evidence_signal: On 72 branching prefixes, generated plans achieved 6.0% RFES with zero observed mean regret versus 8.2% and 0.068 regret for Matched Top-One; separately, schema-based cached-TTS speech achieved task-level RFES on 21/30 simulated voice tasks.
watch_item: Planner latency limits generated-plan deployment, while schema-based results rely on structured candidates and cached TTS in a small simulation.
paper_title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech
